photos.title: On March 11, 889, a 22-year-old Japanese emperor wrote in his diary about a new black cat he had recently acquired… “On the 6th Day of the 2nd Month of the First Year of the Kampo era. Taking a moment of my free time, I
photos.selftext: On March 11, 889, a 22-year-old Japanese emperor wrote in his diary about a new black cat he had recently acquired… “On the 6th Day of the 2nd Month of the First Year of the Kampo era. Taking a moment of my free time, I wish to express my joy of the cat. It arrived by boat as a gift to the late Emperor, received from the hands of Minamoto no Kuwashi. The color of the fur is peerless. None could find the words to describe it, although one said it was reminiscent of the deepest ink. It has an air about it, similar to Kanno. Its length is 5 sun, and its height is 6 sun. I affixed a bow about its neck, but it did not remain for long. In rebellion, it narrows its eyes and extends its needles. It shows its back. When it lies down, it curls in a circle like a coin. You cannot see its feet. It's as if it were circular Bi disk. When it stands, its cry expresses profound loneliness, like a black dragon floating above the clouds. By nature, it likes to stalk birds. It lowers its head and works its tail. It can extend its spine to raise its height by at least 2 sun. Its color allows it to disappear at night. I am convinced it is superior to all other cats.”

photos.title: In 2015, a Virginia jury awarded $500,000 to a patient whose phone accidentally recorded his medical team while he was under sedation. He had intended to record his doctor’s post-procedure instructions, but the recording
photos.selftext: In 2015, a Virginia jury awarded $500,000 to a patient whose phone accidentally recorded his medical team while he was under sedation. He had intended to record his doctor’s post-procedure instructions, but the recording captured anesthesiologist Tiffany Ingham and gastroenterologist Soloman Shah making disparaging remarks about him. The audio reportedly included insults about his intelligence, a false claim that he had syphilis, and comments about avoiding him after the procedure. The case ultimately resulted in an award for defamation, medical malpractice, and punitive damages.

photos.title: Waitress Melina Salazar spent nearly seven years serving a notoriously rude customer who never left her a tip. When he died, she discovered that despite his behavior, he had named her in his will and left her $50,000. Fo
photos.selftext: Waitress Melina Salazar spent nearly seven years serving a notoriously rude customer who never left her a tip. When he died, she discovered that despite his behavior, he had named her in his will and left her $50,000. For nearly seven years, waitress Melina Salazar was the only server at a Luby’s Cafeteria in Brownsville, Texas, willing to regularly serve Walter “Buck” Swords. The 89-year-old World War II veteran had a reputation for being difficult, often cursing at staff, complaining about his meals, and insisting that his food be served extremely hot. He never left a tip. When Swords died in 2007, Salazar received an unexpected surprise. His estate lawyer informed her that Swords had left her $50,000 in cash and his 2000 Buick in his will, reportedly as a thank-you for the patience and kindness she had shown him over the years.

photos.selftext: A woman allegedly stole at least $4 billion, boarded a plane in 2017, and disappeared. Nearly a decade later, the FBI still hasn’t found her. Ruja Ignatova, known as the “Cryptoqueen,” vanished in 2017 after allegedly defrauding investors of billions through her fraudulent cryptocurrency, OneCoin. After learning that her American boyfriend was cooperating with the FBI, she flew from Sofia, Bulgaria, to Athens, Greece, and disappeared without a trace. She remains the only woman on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list.

photos.title: Metallica’s new multimillion-dollar foundation funds trade school across the U.S. It has let tens of thousands of people gain skills without crushing debt. Metallica is famous for heavy metal. For several years the band
photos.selftext: Metallica’s new multimillion-dollar foundation funds trade school across the U.S. It has let tens of thousands of people gain skills without crushing debt. Metallica is famous for heavy metal. For several years the band has also been quietly financing training. Through its nonprofit, All Within My Hands, it has committed more than $17 million to trade programs in the United States. A 2019 pilot at ten community colleges grew into the Metallica Scholars Initiative. By mid-2026 the program reached students at 93 community colleges in all 50 states and Guam. It has helped tens of thousands of people learn high-demand trades without taking on debt. The money supports hands-on programs such as welding, advanced manufacturing, health care, automotive repair, and firefighting. Besides tuition, the foundation pays for safety gear, course materials, and basics such as transportation so students can finish. Band members, including James Hetfield, have said they take pride in raising the standing of trade work and in careers that can support a family. In 2026 the initiative made its first international grant, in the United Kingdom. The band is as serious about the workforce as it is about the stage. [All Within My Hands. (2026). Metallica Scholars Initiative National Workforce Education Program Expands to Over 90 Schools. All Within My Hands Foundation]

photos.selftext: How B.J. Novak’s face ended up on random products around the world.. A few years ago, someone mistakenly uploaded a photo of B.J. Novak, best known for playing Ryan Howard on The Office, to a public-domain website. Because the image was now freely available, it ended up being used on all kinds of random products around the world. When Novak eventually discovered what had happened, he reportedly found the situation more amusing than frustrating, saying, “I am too amused to do anything about it.”
